source: docs/implementation-plan.md#I-076 (PMU and event consistency) mapped onto rtl/core/mosaic_core.sv's observation points; measured by tests/unit/registry.json case pmu.trace_accounting. Widths are the RTL port widths; the p1 build's cache geometry (64 B line, 32 sets, 4 ways) is what the MPKI hand count uses.
comment: CSR-visible rows are architectural and an ISA reference can reproduce them. Every other row is implementation observability: it is debug-only, not readable through a CSR, and no ISA reference produces it. The case prints this same classification so a debug counter is never listed among architectural evidence.

counters.name: minstret
counters.event: an instruction retires
counters.reconciled_by: the program reads minstret by CSRR at two points; each value must equal that CSRR's index in the retire trace, and the delta the instructions between them
counters.description: The Zicntr retired-instruction counter, and the one counter in this mapping an ISA reference reproduces. Both retire lanes are counted: a dual-retire cycle advances it by two (I-076 fixed a single-lane wiring that under-counted every such cycle).

counters.name: mcycle
counters.event: a core clock cycle elapses
counters.reconciled_by: reported as the run's cycle count; the architectural value is the DUT's own cycle counter
counters.description: The Zicntr cycle counter. Not hand-counted (cycle count is a timing property, not a program property); stated architectural and reference-comparable.

counters.name: cycle
counters.event: a core clock cycle elapses (read-only shadow of mcycle)
counters.reconciled_by: read-only shadow; equals mcycle
counters.description: The unprivileged view of mcycle, gated by mcounteren in U/S mode.

counters.name: time
counters.event: the platform mtime input advances a tick
counters.reconciled_by: not exercised: this case holds mtime at zero
counters.description: The Zicntr time counter, sourced from the platform's mtime input rather than from a core counter.

counters.name: zihpm_counter_shadow
counters.event: none -- reads back zero
counters.reconciled_by: the case asserts the Zihpm range decodes but is not a mapping of these event counters
counters.description: Zihpm is advertised (hpmcounter3..31 at 0xc03..0xc1f decode as implemented), but this build answers read-only zero. It is a discoverable shadow, not the event counters below.

counters.name: retired_instructions_debug
counters.event: an instruction retires (debug counter)
counters.reconciled_by: == the hand total (48) for both phases, and == the retire-trace length
counters.description: The debug companion to minstret. It is the number the retire-trace classification is compared against.

counters.name: dispatched_macros
counters.event: a decoded macro is dispatched
counters.reconciled_by: reported; bounded below by the retired count
counters.description: Macros that left the decode queue for the issue queues.

counters.name: uop_insert
counters.event: a uop is inserted into an issue queue
counters.reconciled_by: insert == issue + kill + live IQ occupancy (mosaic_iq's exactly-once conservation)
counters.description: The sum over both clusters of the IQ insertion counter.

counters.name: uop_issue
counters.event: a uop is granted an execution unit
counters.reconciled_by: part of the uop conservation identity
counters.description: The sum over both clusters of the IQ grant counter.

counters.name: uop_kill
counters.event: a uop is killed in an issue queue by a redirect
counters.reconciled_by: part of the uop conservation identity
counters.description: The sum over both clusters of the IQ kill counter.

counters.name: dcache_txn
counters.event: the L1D accepts a CPU request
counters.reconciled_by: cache_on: == hand memory operations (10); == hit + miss
counters.description: Loads and stores the data cache accepted. Zero when the cache is disabled.

counters.name: dcache_hit
counters.event: an accepted CPU request is served from a present line
counters.reconciled_by: cache_on: == hand (7); hit + miss == txn
counters.description: The hit half of the data-cache request decomposition.

counters.name: dcache_miss
counters.event: an accepted CPU request misses
counters.reconciled_by: cache_on: == hand distinct cold lines (3); MPKI numerator
counters.description: The miss half of the data-cache request decomposition; MPKI = this / retired * 1000 = 62.50.

counters.name: dcache_refill
counters.event: the L1D starts a line fill
counters.reconciled_by: cache_on: refill == miss (a demand miss starts one fill)
counters.description: Line fills requested from memory for demand accesses.

counters.name: dcache_writeback
counters.event: the L1D writes back a dirty line
counters.reconciled_by: cache_on: == hand dirty lines flushed (2: DATA_B and TOHOST)
counters.description: Dirty lines written back; the FENCE.I before the park flushes them.

counters.name: icache_miss
counters.event: an instruction fetch misses the L1I
counters.reconciled_by: reported; the instruction side of MPKI
counters.description: Instruction-side misses, a separate observation point from the LSU's.

counters.name: wb_writes
counters.event: the writeback arbiter writes a destination
counters.reconciled_by: == the trace's retiring register-write count (37)
counters.description: Physical-register writes published by the arbiters.

counters.name: wb_collision
counters.event: two producers collide on a writeback port
counters.reconciled_by: reported; zero for this program
counters.description: The WB-conflict counter the card names.

counters.name: wb_wakeup
counters.event: the arbiter publishes a wakeup
counters.reconciled_by: reported
counters.description: Wakeups issued by the writeback arbiters.

counters.name: lq_alloc
counters.event: a load allocates a load-queue entry
counters.reconciled_by: == the trace's load count; done + occupied <= alloc
counters.description: Load-queue allocations.

counters.name: lq_done
counters.event: a load completes
counters.reconciled_by: == the hand load count (6)
counters.description: Loads that completed and returned to the ROB.

counters.name: lq_replay
counters.event: a load is replayed
counters.reconciled_by: reported; zero for this program
counters.description: The replay counter the card names, on the load path.

counters.name: sq_alloc
counters.event: a store allocates a store-queue entry
counters.reconciled_by: alloc == drain + squash + occupied (mosaic_store_queue conservation)
counters.description: Store-queue allocations.

counters.name: sq_drain
counters.event: a committed store drains to memory
counters.reconciled_by: == the hand store count (4)
counters.description: Committed stores that reached memory.

counters.name: sq_squash
counters.event: a speculative store is squashed
counters.reconciled_by: part of the store-queue conservation identity
counters.description: Stores killed before commit; the double-count control's target in the store domain.

counters.name: lsu_txn
counters.event: the LSU endpoint accepts a memory transaction
counters.reconciled_by: cache_off: == hand memory operations (10)
counters.description: Endpoint transactions; with the cache on the misses (and PTW reads) are the only ones that reach it.

counters.name: lq_mem_bytes
counters.event: a load's bytes come from memory rather than from forwarding
counters.reconciled_by: reported
counters.description: Load bytes served by memory (as opposed to store-to-load forwarding).

counters.name: dispatch_occupancy_sum
counters.event: one cycle at the decode queue's depth
counters.reconciled_by: <= depth * cycles; mean depth = sum / cycles
counters.description: Cycle-integrated occupancy of the decode queue.

counters.name: iq_occupancy_sum
counters.event: one cycle at the two issue queues' combined depth
counters.reconciled_by: <= 2 * iq_entries * cycles; mean depth = sum / cycles
counters.description: Cycle-integrated occupancy of both issue queues.

counters.name: iqueue_occupancy_sum
counters.event: one cycle at the decoded-instruction queue's depth
counters.reconciled_by: <= depth * cycles; mean depth = sum / cycles
counters.description: Cycle-integrated occupancy of the decoded-instruction queue.

counters.name: fetch_request
counters.event: the front end offers an instruction request
counters.reconciled_by: cache_off: == the harness's own instruction-beat count
counters.description: Fetch requests, cross-checked against the driver's bus count.

counters.name: fetch_response
counters.event: the front end receives an instruction response
counters.reconciled_by: reported
counters.description: Fetch responses accepted.

counters.name: redirect
counters.event: the front end redirects
counters.reconciled_by: reported; the control's double-count is injected per redirect
counters.description: Redirects, including the branch-barrier redirects this recovery model performs on every taken branch.

counters.name: recover_cycles
counters.event: one cycle spent in the recovery barrier
counters.reconciled_by: reported
counters.description: Cycles the front end was held by recovery.

counters.name: barrier_cycles
counters.event: one cycle with a branch in flight or the core halted
counters.reconciled_by: reported
counters.description: Cycles the allocation barrier held.

counters.name: vector_elements
counters.event: a vector element retires
counters.reconciled_by: not exercised by this p1 scalar program
counters.description: Useful elements the card names. Present as a port; the case's program is scalar, so it is reported as not exercised.

counters.name: lane_elements
counters.event: a lane publishes a vector element
counters.reconciled_by: not exercised by this p1 scalar program
counters.description: Eight 32-bit per-lane element counts.

counters.name: fabric_grant
counters.event: the steering fabric grants a macro a route
counters.reconciled_by: reported; this is local cross-cluster routing, not remote-coherence traffic
counters.description: The nearest thing this single-hart core has to the card's remote traffic, and it is explicitly not remote traffic (see not_covered).

counters.name: fabric_stall
counters.event: a macro waits for a route
counters.reconciled_by: reported
counters.description: A stall-reason counter from the steering fabric.

not_covered: Remote/coherence link traffic: the p0/p1 single-hart core has no remote link endpoint, so the card's remote-traffic item is mapped to o_fab_grant_ctr (local cross-cluster steering) and said so; the true remote/coherence counters belong to the I-029/I-030 fabric, not to this case.
Vector IPC versus scalar IPC as a speed judgement (the card's first named anti-pattern): this case counts retired work and cache events, never compares IPC; performance comparison is I-077/I-084.
Toggle counts presented as measured power (the card's second named anti-pattern): no switching-activity counter is exported, and none is reported as power.
Zihpm as a mapping of these events: the profile decodes hpmcounter3..31 but this build reads them as zero, so the event counters above are not architectural and are not presented as such.
FP event counters (o_fp_issue/commit/flags/merge) and the full vector element/chain counters: present as ports and not exercised by the p1 scalar program of this case.
The p0 cacheless build's cache counters: p0 claims no cache, so the case runs on p1 and the cache-phase numbers are p1's geometry.
